title: Tested, not vibed: GTM writing evals
tagline: Testing which of the instructions behind AI-written GTM copy beat saying nothing, with a public suite anyone can re-run.
phase: Week 1 of 7: pre-registration due 14 November; the source check is done, one decision and Alex's signature remain
why: The pipeline writes every post, note and brief from a style guide of more than 100 guidance lines. As of 8 November 2026, none of them had been run against a no-guidance control (first-party check of the pipeline repo), so nobody can say which lines change the output.
mission: AO-EVAL-SUITE, a public, re-runnable eval suite for GTM agent writing, aimed at Alex's own rulebook. It screens failure types against a no-guidance control, then tests rule wordings only where the control fails. The types come from his written corrections, or from the rules he wrote down when his corrections are too thin to rank. Alongside it, an audit of every rule and a backfill of debriefs for attended rooms that never got one.
destination: A pre-registered study published with its raw samples, grader code and agreement between graders, so a stranger can re-run it. The rulebook keeps only the rules that beat saying nothing, and the count of rules tested appears on this page as a metric. Anyone can check by re-running the suite.
showcase: Designing a behaviour eval the way a lab would (designed, not yet run): pre-registration before the first sample, a no-guidance control, yes/no graders and a rep count set for statistical power
Screening many failure types against the control first instead of hand-picking test cases, with a written ranking rule that lets the author remove a type for one stated reason but never add one
Measuring the sampling rate before committing to the design, and counting every retry in the data that will be published instead of only the successes
Sizing a build by two budgets: the hours only Alex can give (decisions, labels, reads) and the hours agents can run overnight
Applying a method from software engineering (test the instruction against its absence first) to sales and marketing writing

milestones.note: Branch 2 is what the written procedure already says: review comments came back under its floor of 60, so its fallback applies, the anti-patterns file in file order. That needs three changes made after seeing data, each logged as a deviation: a new source (his working sessions with the drafting agent), a floor counted in corrections rather than comments, and a random label sample instead of the first 50. Even then, a check on 11 November found no type that clears the eligibility rule of 5 corrections on 3 drafts: 72 corrections in 1,663 messages sent before 8 November; with the review comments, the candidate corrections fall into 34 types.

decisions.decision: Adopt the testing method, not the borrowed skills: an instruction stays only if it beats saying nothing.
decisions.why: Imported skills were written for coding agents. The method transfers to writing, the wording doesn't.

decisions.decision: Screen many failure types against a control instead of hand-picking two test cases.
decisions.why: Picking the cases yourself biases the study, and two small cases make the whole result hang on chance.

decisions.decision: Backfilled debriefs write only to the private knowledge graph (Notion event records and the private claims store). Drafts, outreach and CRM records stay out of the backfill, and every backfilled claim is tagged as backfill (by design).
decisions.why: Rooms debriefed weeks later are useful context, but they shouldn't read as first-hand records.

decisions.decision: Make no claim of being first until the write-up publishes with its prior-art section.
decisions.why: A claim of being first is only as strong as the search behind it, and that search belongs in the public write-up.

decisions.decision: Plan signed off: five lanes run at once, with agents building and running the samples, and the study design approved ahead of the written pre-registration.
decisions.why: The proof has to be public before the end-of-year window, and the sampling runs overnight on agent hours, not Alex's.

decisions.decision: The sampler retries an empty or failed output up to twice, and every retry is counted in the published data.
decisions.why: The first timed run lost 2 of 100 samples silently. Dropping them quietly would bias the results; hiding the retries would overstate reliability.

decisions.decision: Page convention, set by the author (not a study decision): health is called against written criteria. On track: every dated gate is on its date, no gate due within 7 days waits on an open decision or input, and no kill rule has fired. At risk: a gate due within 7 days waits on an open decision or input, or a forecast slip is absorbed by the stated slack (the 12 December write-up date holds); the page then names the path back to on track and its date. Off track: a dated gate has passed without a new date, a kill rule has fired, or 12 December can no longer hold. The most cautious reading governs, and an at-risk call that can't be justified is reported as off track.
decisions.why: A colour without pre-agreed criteria is a mood. Written criteria let a reader check the call. They were written on 11 November, after the first at-risk call on 10 November; that call was rechecked against them and holds.

open.question: Pick the failure-type source. Branch 2: the written fallback, the anti-patterns file in file order. Branch 1: Alex's own corrections, which needs a new source, a new floor and a new label sample, each logged as a deviation, and still found no eligible type on 11 November.
open.unblocks: The failure-type list and the signature
open.recommendation: Branch 2, signed as written, with the write-up saying the corrections record was too thin to rank.

open.question: Only if branch 1 is picked: label 50 corrections drawn at random from the 72 found in his sessions (instead of the first 50 review comments), so the classifier's agreement can be reported against a majority-class baseline. Starts after the branch pick; otherwise it serves the proposed run 2.
open.recommendation: Skip for run 1 if branch 2 is chosen.

open.question: Sign the pre-registration: confirm the failure-type list, state a prediction before any sample, and pick the marketplace GTM skill tested as one of the arms.
Where AO-EVAL-SUITE lives: its own public repo (recommended), or a folder in an existing one. Also its licence.
Whether the style-guide update loop should also read his working sessions: it reads review comments, but since September his corrections have mostly happened in conversation.
open.unblocks: Run 2's source, and the rulebook audit

risks.risk: Issue, live since 11 November: the review-comment export came back with 17 countable comments on 6 of 935 drafts, under the 60 the selection procedure needs, so its written fallback applies (the anti-patterns file in file order). A second check, of Alex's working sessions, found no type that clears the eligibility rule. The failure-type list and the 14 November signature wait on Alex picking branch 1 or 2.
risks.mitigation: Path to green: Alex picks a branch (branch 2 recommended), any change is logged as a deviation with its reason, and the pre-registration is signed by 14 November. If 14 November passes unsigned, every later date moves day for day and the health call goes to off track under the written criteria.

risks.risk: Risk: the 14 November sign date slips for any other reason. Trigger: no signed, hashed pre-registration by the end of 14 November. Owner: Alex.
risks.mitigation: No study sample is generated before the signature, whatever the date. The screen and the full run move day for day; the 12 December write-up keeps its slack because the whole study needs under an hour of sampling.

risks.risk: Risk: no failure type fails the control often enough to test, so there is nothing to compare. Trigger, pre-written in the draft pre-registration: by 22 November no type has at least 5 failures in 16 control samples with at least 12 of them gradable. Owner: Alex.
risks.mitigation: The null-result note is written into the draft pre-registration and freezes when it is signed. A short null note then publishes, with every cell's count and denominator, and the hours move to the other lanes. A null is a result.

risks.risk: Risk: fewer than two outside graders by 5 December. Trigger: confirmed graders under two on that date. Owner: Alex.
risks.mitigation: Pre-agreed in the draft pre-registration: publish with author grading only and say so on the results page. The grader-agreement number is then absent, not estimated.

risks.risk: Risk: the author wrote the rules, the failure cases and the grader, so a positive result could just be the author agreeing with himself.
risks.mitigation: By design: pre-registration before the first sample, yes/no checks graded by code where possible, a blind grader that never sees the style guide, raw samples published, and outside graders whose agreement is reported.

risks.risk: Assumption: the subscription allows the full study to run across the planned nights: at most about 1,030 study samples (768 in the main design, up to 256 more for the second-model check), plus retries and one grader call per sample. Its daily ceiling has not been measured; the 100-sample timed test is the only datapoint.
risks.mitigation: If it binds, the study runs over more nights: at the measured rate even about 2,000 calls take under an hour. The pre-registration's fixed sample counts do not change.

risks.risk: Risk: backfilled debriefs written weeks after the event could read as fact to later runs.
risks.mitigation: Every backfilled claim is tagged as backfill and stored as an unreviewed candidate, which later runs see flagged as unreviewed rather than as approved fact. Nothing public is written from a backfilled event.

log.text: Second source checked before signing: 1,663 messages from Alex's working sessions sent before 8 November held 72 corrections; with the review comments, the candidates fall into 34 types, none clearing the eligibility rule of 5 corrections on 3 drafts. Most sessions from before mid-September no longer exist. The source decision now has two written branches, and a second run in January is proposed. Health stays at risk until the signature. Debrief backfill wave 1 finished early: three rooms, 223 claims stored as unreviewed candidates.

Comment export finished: 17 countable comments by Alex on 6 of 935 drafts, under the 60 the selection procedure needs. Its written fallback applies, and whether to keep or amend it is now an open decision before the 14 November sign date. Health stays at risk, unchanged since 10 November; the path to green is that decision plus the signature by 14 November. Health criteria written onto this page.

Sampling throughput measured: 100 of 100 samples (4 after one retry) in 150 seconds, about 2,400 an hour against a floor of 60. Suite scaffolded, pre-registration drafted, and the export of review comments started for choosing failure types. Health called at risk: the sign date depends on Alex's labels and sign-off.
Plan rewritten at full scale, claims checked against prior art and narrowed, and the plan signed off.
First plan written, red-teamed and shared for review.
Attended a talk on test-first agent instructions, which started the project.
